headline: AMVUTTRA drives revenue surge as sequential profit eases
summary_short: Q2 revenue jumped 67% y/y to $1,291M, swinging Alnylam to a $164M profit from a year-ago loss, though net income and diluted EPS ($1.21) each fell about 20% versus Q1 as R&D and SG&A spending stepped up.
summary_long: Net product revenue rose 74% to $1,172M, led by AMVUTTRA (+106% to $1,012M) on higher U.S. ATTR-CM demand, partly offset by declining ONPATTRO sales; GIVLAARI and OXLUMO also grew. Royalty revenue rose 79% on higher Leqvio sales by Novartis; collaboration revenue fell 23% as the Regeneron research term wound down. Cost of goods sold rose to 25.4% of product revenue (from 21.1%) on AMVUTTRA's higher blended Sanofi royalty rate. R&D and SG&A both rose on higher clinical-trial and commercial-launch spending. Cash stood at $1,708M; no quantified forward guidance was disclosed this quarter.

drivers.explanation: Revenue and profit growth was driven by AMVUTTRA's continued ATTR-CM launch and higher royalty revenue from Novartis's Leqvio sales, partly offset by lower Regeneron collaboration revenue and higher R&D/SG&A spend on late-stage trials and the AMVUTTRA launch.
Net product revenues grew mainly on AMVUTTRA demand growth from ATTR-CM patients in the U.S. and increased GIVLAARI/OXLUMO patients, partly offset by fewer ONPATTRO patients.
Cost of goods sold rose to 25.4% of net product revenue (from 21.1%) on higher AMVUTTRA sales and an increased blended royalty rate owed to Sanofi.
Operating cash flow rose on stronger product-sales receipts, partly offset by higher employee compensation; investing outflows grew on securities-purchase timing and higher capex.
